align.prompt: Run the llm-straighten and llm-network-loop LLM ablation baselines for as-twn-taipei, variant orig-llm-working2grid-opus5, as a forced re-run from scratch: reset each chain first, then decide every grid coordinate by hand-reasoning (no algorithm), and make sure a complete, rule-compliant assignment is actually applied rather than handing back an analysis.

transcript.note: Round 1. Method: I first built the lock table from hvSegs (a V segment locks that vertex's column, an H segment locks its row), which leaves only 14 of the 59 vertices with a usable free axis. I then worked each of the 20 offSegs and only proposed a move where the free axis of one endpoint could reach the other endpoint's locked row/col. Six one-axis snaps buy H/V outright: 43->(12,26) and 29->(16,51) and 50->(20,57) are degree-1 stubs sliding onto their partner's row; 26->(35,46) drops onto 27's locked row 46 and lengthens the col-35 trunk instead of bending it; 34->(54,27) joins the col-54 trunk so 34-55 becomes V; 16->(31,34) slides along its locked row 34 onto 58's locked col 31 (chosen over col 28, which would have given two 45deg instead of one V -- HV is the primary key, so the V wins). Two vertices with two free cols meet in the middle: 2->(34,12) with 3->(34,4) makes 2-3 vertical AND leaves 2-18 at exactly (-3,+3) = 45deg, a two-for-one that col 35 or 36 would not give. The one unblocking move: 45-20 could not become horizontal because stub 0 sat at (23,15) right on the line and would have been swallowed (hard rule 3), so I re-hung 0 northward as a vertical stub at (25,12) and pulled 20 two cols west to (25,15) -- that keeps 0 H/V, makes 45-20 horizontal, and as a bonus puts 23-20 at exactly (-10,-10) = 45deg. For 38 I compared row 21 (45deg on 13-38) against row 15 (H on 38-18) and took row 15: +1 HV beats +1 HVD lexicographically even though it costs the 13-38 diagonal. Where H/V was unreachable within a short move I settled for 45deg: 4->(14,7) is a one-cell nudge onto the exact diagonal between 47(7,0) and 35(20,13), so BOTH of 4's segments become 45deg at once; 42->(27,40) puts the dangling terminus on 39's diagonal (row 34 is impossible -- cell (20,34) is occupied and any other row-34 target would swallow vertex 16). I left 45-36, 36-23, 38-12 and 16-33 alone: all four have both endpoints locked on both axes, and the only group move that could free 36-23 (dragging the whole row-25 chain 23/12/22/46 down to row 27) collides with 40 at (42,27). Pre-verified the whole batch against my own mirror of the crossing / swallow / collide / winding-order checks before spending the round: cross 0->0, vtxOn 0->0, collide 0, no winding violations.

Round 2. All five still-unaligned segments (45-36, 36-23, 13-38, 38-12, 16-33) now have BOTH endpoints locked on BOTH axes, so nothing further is reachable by moving one vertex -- this round is entirely about group moves and about upgrading 45deg to H/V, which is where the remaining score is. (a) 47 and 35 both hang off 4 (Dingpu) with no H/V segment of their own, so the 47-4-35 chain was a clean 45deg staircase. Sliding 35 to (20,7) and 47 to (7,7) puts all three on row 7: two diagonals become two horizontals, +2 HV. I checked the alternatives first -- moving 4 alone to row 13 or col 20 also gives one H/V but destroys the other diagonal, so it nets +1 HV -1 HVD; lining the chain up beats both. 47-8 shortens to a single cell, which is legal and common in schematic drawings. (b) 16-33 is at (-11,-8) and cannot be H/V at all: row 34 for 33 is cell (20,34), already taken by 15, and putting 33 on col 31 would break both of its V segments. 45deg needs dy = -11, i.e. 33 on row 23, but 33's row is pinned by the 33-43 horizontal -- so I moved the pair rigidly, 33 to (20,23) with its degree-1 partner 43 to (12,23). 33-43 stays horizontal, both col-20 V segments survive (order on col 20 stays 35 < 45 < 33 < 15), and 16-33 becomes exactly (-11,-11) = 45deg. (c) Things I costed out and rejected: dragging the whole row-27 chain (36/44/40/17/34) down one row would make 45-36 a 45deg but breaks the 44-58 diagonal, net zero; sliding the row-15 chain (45/20/18/38/53/54) up one row likewise gains 45-36 but loses both 2-18 and 23-20, net -1; making 13-38 a 45deg needs the col-44 chain (21/6/13) moved six columns west, which reverses 6 against its stub 5. I also left 42 (Luzhou) on its 45deg instead of pulling it to col 33 for a third HV: that is a six-cell move, outside the short-distance rule, and Luzhou really is north-WEST of Daqiaotou, so the diagonal is the faithful bearing. Pre-verified: cross 0->0, vtxOn 0->0, collide 0, no winding-order violations.

Round 3, and I expect it to be the last useful one. Four segments are still unaligned (45-36, 36-23, 13-38, 38-12) and every endpoint of all four is locked on both axes, so the only lever left is a rigid translation of a whole locked chain. 45-36 sits at (11,12) -- one row short of a perfect 45deg. Pulling 36 alone to row 26 is impossible (36-44 pins its row), so I translated the entire row-27 trunk down one row: 36/44/40/17/34 -> row 26. That alone would have cost me the 44-58 diagonal, which drops from (-4,4) to (-4,5), so I translated the row-31 trunk down one row in step with it: 58/24/10/30/41 -> row 30. The two shifts cancel exactly -- 44-58 stays at (-4,4) -- and 45-36 lands on (11,11) = 45deg. Everything hanging off the two trunks survives because only the shared row changes, never a column: 36-58, 44-23, 44-24, 40-12, 40-10, 17-22, 17-30, 34-55, 24-25, 10-9, 31-30, 55-32 are all vertical and keep their columns, and each column's top-to-bottom order is preserved (col 35 stays 23 < 44 < 24 < 25, col 42 stays 12 < 40 < 10 < 9, col 45 stays 22 < 17 < 30 < 31). This is a rigid move, so it is exactly the case the rules allow: 10 vertices, one row each, and my pre-check confirms it -- orderFlip 0, maxDrift 0.018, cross 0, vtxOn 0, no winding-order violations. I also costed the two remaining candidates and both come out net zero, so I am not proposing them: translating the row-25 chain (23/12/22/46) up two rows makes 36-23 a 45deg but breaks 23-20, and moving the col-44 chain (21/6/13, plus stub 5 which rule 2 would otherwise veto) six columns west makes 13-38 a 45deg at the price of shoving the whole Xindian branch off its relative position. 38-12 at (7,10) has no reachable alignment at all. So H/V should stop at 65/74 with 71/74 aligned once 45deg is counted.
